data.title: Fiji declares state of disaster amid El Nino-driven drought
data.description:
Fiji has declared a national state of disaster after an El Nino-driven drought caused widespread water shortages, with the Pacific nation's weather bureau forecasting below-normal rainfall until at least April.

In a national address on Wednesday, Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka said the declaration would allow his government to scale up its response by mobilising resources and coordinating assistance as conditions continue to worsen.

"Families across Fiji are concerned about the availability of water and the effects of prolonged dry conditions on their daily lives," Rabuka said.

"Farmers are worried about their crops and livestock, while communities, particularly in remote and maritime areas, face growing pressure on their water supplies. These concerns are real."

Rabuka said his government has set aside 20 million Fiji dollars ($8.5 million) for the national response, redeployed from existing funds, to ensure emergency water supplies for families and farmers.

The state of disaster has been declared for one month, with the government able to extend or revoke it based on the advice of the National Disaster Risk Management Council.

El Nino is a natural climate pattern in which surface temperatures in the central and eastern Pacific Ocean become unusually warm, causing weather extremes around the world, including drought in some regions and flooding in others. Some scientists say global warming may increase its intensity.

The US Climate Prediction Center said last week that El Nino is strengthening, with a greater than 79% chance of a strong-to-very-strong event through January to March. Australia in June said El Nino could intensify in the second half of 2026 to become one of the strongest in seven decades.

Fiji's national weather bureau warned in October that strong El Nino conditions persist across the tropical Pacific.

Rainfall is likely to remain below normal from November through April, while daytime temperatures are expected to exceed normal levels through January across most of the country, the Fiji Meteorological Service said.

($1 = 2.3436 Fiji dollars)

data.title: Emmaus Life Sciences Reports Quarterly Financial Results
data.description:
Emmaus Life Sciences, Inc. (OTCQB: EMMA), a commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company and leader in the treatment of sickle cell disease, today reported on its financial condition and results of operations as of and for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026.

Highlights

“Our global net revenues declined for the three months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to the same period in 2025 primarily driven by a 44% decrease in U.S. net revenues as our licensing agreement with NeoImmuneTech Inc. (NIT), became effective on May 15, 2026,” commented Willis Lee, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Emmaus. “The decline was partially offset by a related reduction in our operating expenses. Management believes that the conflict in the Middle East also adversely affected net revenues in the region,” he added.

Financial and Operating Results

Net Revenues. Net revenues for the three months ended September 30, 2026 were $1.9 million, compared to $3.4 million in the same period in 2025 driven by lower direct sales of Endari® following the company’s execution of the License Agreement with NIT.

Operating Expenses. Total operating expenses for the three months were $1.9 million compared to $2.4 million in the comparable period in 2025. The decrease was due primarily to decreased expenses attributable to the transfer of our sales force to NIT in connection with the license arrangement.

Income (Loss) From Operations. Loss from operations for the three months was $0.4 million compared to income from operations of $0.7 million in the same period in 2025. The changes were due to the decrease in net revenues, partially offset by lower operating expenses.

Other Expense. The company realized other expense of $4.4 million for the three months compared to $2.2 million in the same period in 2025. The increase was primarily due to change in fair value of conversion features derivative based upon an increase in the company’s stock price.

Net Loss. For the three months, the company realized a net loss of $4.7 million, or $0.07 basic loss per share based on approximately 70.2 million weighted-average common shares, compared to net loss of $2.1 million, or $0.03 basic loss per share based on approximately 63.9 million weighted-average common shares in the comparable period in 2025. The increase in net loss was attributable primarily to the decrease in net revenues and increase in other expense.

Liquidity and Capital Resources. At September 30, 2026, the company had cash and cash equivalents of $1.0 million, compared to $2.1 million at December 31, 2025.

About Emmaus Life Sciences

Emmaus Life Sciences, Inc. is a commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company and leader in the treatment of sickle cell disease. Endari® (L-glutamine oral powder), indicated to reduce the acute complications of sickle cell disease in adults and children 5 years and older, is approved for marketing in the United States, Israel, Kuwait, Qatar, the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain and Oman and is available on a named patient or early access basis in France, the Netherlands, and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, where Emmaus’ application for marketing authorization is awaiting final action by the Saudi Food & Drug Authority. For more information, please visit www.emmausmedical.com.

About Endari® (prescription grade L-glutamine oral powder)

Endari®, Emmaus’ prescription grade L-glutamine oral powder, was approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in July 2017 for treating sickle cell disease in adult and pediatric patients five years of age and older.

Indication

Endari® is indicated to reduce the acute complications of sickle cell disease in adult and pediatric patients five years of age and older.

Important Safety Information

The most common adverse reactions (incidence >10 percent) in clinical studies were constipation, nausea, headache, abdominal pain, cough, pain in extremities, back pain, and chest pain.

Adverse reactions leading to treatment discontinuation included one case each of hypersplenism, abdominal pain, dyspepsia, burning sensation, and hot flash.

The safety and efficacy of Endari® in pediatric patients with sickle cell disease younger than five years of age has not been established.

For more information, please see full Prescribing Information of Endari® at: www.ENDARIrx.com/PI.

About Sickle Cell Disease

There are approximately 100,000 people living with sickle cell disease (SCD) in the United States and millions more globally. The sickle gene is found in every ethnic group, not just among those of African descent; and in the United States an estimated 1-in-365 African Americans and 1-in-16,300 Hispanic Americans are born with SCD.1 The genetic mutation responsible for SCD causes an individual's red blood cells to distort into a "C" or a sickle shape, reducing their ability to transport oxygen throughout the body. These sickled red blood cells break down rapidly, become very sticky, and develop a propensity to clump together, which causes them to become stuck and cause damage within blood vessels. The result is reduced blood flow to distal organs, which leads to physical symptoms of incapacitating pain, tissue and organ damage, and early death.2

1Source: Data & Statistics on Sickle Cell Disease – National Center on Birth Defects and Developmental Disabilities, Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, December 2020.

2Source: Committee on Addressing Sickle Cell Disease – A Strategic Plan and Blueprint for Action -- National Academy of Sciences Press, 2020.

Forward-looking Statements

This press release contains forward-looking statements made pursuant to the safe harbor provisions of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995, as amended. These forward-looking statements are subject to numerous assumptions, risks and uncertainties which change over time, including doubt about the company’s ability to continue as a going concern and other factors disclosed in the company’s Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025 filed with the SEC on March 31, 2026 and Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q filed on November 18, 2026, and actual results may differ materially. Such forward-looking statements speak only as of the date they are made, and Emmaus assumes no duty to update them, except as may be required by law.

data.title: Gold recovers from one-year low as markets assess Fed rate outlook
data.description:
Gold prices edged higher on Thursday after hitting a more-than-one-year low in the previous session, as investors awaited further signals from the US Federal Reserve for clues on the central bank's monetary policy path.

FUNDAMENTALS

* Spot gold was up 0.6% at $3,745.56 per ounce by 0035 GMT, after hitting a 14-month low on Wednesday. US gold futures for December delivery edged 0.1% higher to $3,746.80.

* Federal Reserve officials saw a growing risk last month that they might need to intensify their efforts to control inflation, even as they agreed to keep interest rates steady for the moment, the minutes of their October 27-28 showed on Wednesday.

* Fed Governor Michael Barr said on Wednesday he's likely to be on board with tighter monetary policy in an economy still beset by inflation pressures.

* Markets see a 90% chance of a 25-basis-point US rate hike in December, while the probability of a larger 50-basis-point move is priced at 10%, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

* Higher interest rates increase the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding bullion, reducing its appeal to investors.

* Elsewhere, the Bank of Japan will raise interest rates for the third time this year at its December meeting and follow up with another by end-March, according to a majority of economists in a Reuters poll.

* The global platinum market will swing back to deficit next year due to higher bar and coin demand and smaller outflows from platinum-backed exchange-traded funds, the World Platinum Investment Council said on Wednesday.

* The United Arab Emirates remained the top destination for smuggled African gold in 2024 despite tightening its rules a year earlier, a report by non-governmental organisation Swissaid said.

* Spot silver climbed 1.3% to $45.61 per ounce, platinum rose 0.71% to $1,381.04 and palladium gained 0.9% to $956.25.

data.title: Walker & Dunlop Arranges $270 Million Refinancing for Nasser Freres’ The Greyson in Jersey City
data.description:
Walker & Dunlop, Inc. announced today that it has arranged $270,000,000 in refinancing for The Greyson, a 28-story, 622-unit, Class A mixed-use residential tower developed by Nasser Freres in the heart of Jersey City's Journal Square neighborhood. The financing marks a significant milestone for the development, supporting its transition from construction to stabilized operations and positioning the property for long-term success.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261118022862/en/

The Greyson. Photo credits: Nasser Freres

Walker & Dunlop Capital Markets Institutional Advisory served as exclusive advisor to Nasser Freres, arranging a floating-rate, interest-only bridge loan from affiliates of Apollo. The transaction was arranged by Keith Kurland, Aaron Appel, Adam Schwartz, Jonathan Schwartz, Jordan Casella, Christopher de Raet, and Jack Krentzman.

"Journal Square has undergone a remarkable transformation, and The Greyson exemplifies the caliber of development attracting investment to the neighborhood,” said Kurland, senior managing director of Capital Markets and co-head of Institutional Advisory at Walker & Dunlop. "With its exceptional location, extensive amenities, and proximity to Manhattan, the property is well-positioned to capitalize on the area’s continued growth. We’re pleased to have worked with Nasser Freres and Apollo to execute this transaction.”

Located at 25 Cottage Street, The Greyson encompasses 424,328 rentable square feet, including 389,328 square feet of residential and 35,000 square feet of commercial space. The property features a collection of studio, one-, two-, and three-bedroom residences with unobstructed views of the Jersey City skyline. Designed to deliver an elevated residential experience, The Greyson offers an extensive suite of amenities, including an art gallery, children's playroom, screening room, gaming lounge, virtual reality and sports room, coffee bar, fitness center, speakeasy, and private event space. Ground-floor retail space leased to a wine bar further enhances the property’s appeal while contributing to Journal Square’s growing dining and entertainment scene.

"From the outset, our vision for The Greyson was to create something truly distinctive, a property that would help shape the next chapter of residential living in Journal Square while contributing meaningfully to the neighborhood’s continued transformation,” said Michael Sokoloff, partner at Nasser Freres. "We’ve been intentional about every aspect of this development, from its architecture and design to the amenities and experiences we’re bringing to residents. We’re incredibly proud of what we’ve built and believe The Greyson will set a new standard for the neighborhood for years to come. This refinancing marks an exciting next chapter as we shift our focus to the property’s long-term success and we appreciate Walker & Dunlop’s advisory.”

Situated along the newly opened Homestead commercial corridor, the property is less than a five-minute walk from the Journal Square Transportation Center, offering direct PATH access to Lower and Midtown Manhattan in approximately 10 and 20 minutes, respectively. Journal Square has emerged as one of the New York metropolitan area's fastest-growing rental submarkets, driven by demand for transit-oriented housing and rental rates that remain comparatively affordable to those along the Jersey City Waterfront and in Manhattan.

In the first half of 2026, Walker & Dunlop’s Capital Markets team sourced over $13.9 billion from non-Agency capital providers, including nearly $9.6 billion for multifamily properties. This vast experience has made them a top advisor on all asset classes for many of the industry’s top developers, owners, and operators. To learn more about Walker & Dunlop’s broad financing options, visit our website.

About Walker & Dunlop

Walker & Dunlop () is one of the largest commercial real estate finance and advisory services firms in the United States and internationally. Our ideas and capital create communities where people live, work, shop, and play. Our innovative people, breadth of our brand, and our technological capabilities make us one of the most insightful and client-focused firms in the commercial real estate industry.

data.title: First Graphene Expands Composites Development into China with UNITEX
data.description:
Highlights

  • Joint Development and Commercialisation Agreement signed with UNITEX Composite (Ningbo) Co., Ltd., part of UNITEX Group, a global materials technology group specialising in advanced composites and integrated material solutions for a wide range of applications, combining development and manufacturing capabilities in China with an established customer network spanning more than 100 countries.
  • Initial focus on graphene enhanced carbon fibre prepreg, with plans to expand into thermoplastics, resin concentrates, coatings and elastomers.
  • Agreement combines First Graphene's formulation and dispersion expertise with UNITEX's manufacturing and innovation capabilities, and established international supply network.
  • Provides First Graphene with a pathway into China's composites manufacturing and innovation sector and access to wider international markets, helping to accelerate the development, scale-up and global commercialisation of graphene-enhanced materials across a broad range of applications.

Sydney, Australia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 18, 2026) - First Graphene Limited  (FSE: M11) (OTCQB: FGPHF) ("First Graphene" or "the Company") is pleased to announce it has entered into a Joint Development and Commercialisation Agreement ("the Agreement") with UNITEX Composite (Ningbo) Co., Ltd. ("UNITEX"), establishing a strategic collaboration to develop and commercialise graphene enhanced carbon fibre composites and other advanced materials.

The Agreement represents a further step in First Graphene's strategy to commercialise its graphene technologies through strategic development and manufacturing partnerships. The collaboration draws on UNITEX's material development, engineering and manufacturing capabilities in China, providing First Graphene with a pathway into China's significant composites manufacturing sector and the international markets it supplies.

Headquartered in Ningbo, China's Zhejiang province, UNITEX is a global materials technology group specialising in advanced composites and integrated material solutions for a wide range of applications. Built on its manufacturing capabilities in China, the group combines material development, application engineering and industrial supply chain integration to translate material technologies into commercially viable products and solutions.

With an established customer network spanning more than 100 countries, UNITEX serves industries including automotive, aerospace, semiconductors, energy, marine, construction and sporting goods.

Its capabilities extend from customised material development and engineering support to industrial-scale manufacturing and global supply, providing a foundation for the international commercialisation of jointly developed materials.

The collaboration will combine First Graphene's expertise in graphene selection, formulation and dispersion with UNITEX's materials engineering, manufacturing infrastructure and established supply chain capabilities.

Development and commercialisation program

The initial development program will focus on graphene enhanced carbon fibre prepreg, building on First Graphene's internal research and development activities, which demonstrated improvements in strength and barrier properties through incorporation of graphene into carbon fibre composites.

Where the results justify further development, the parties intend to progress successful formulations through customer validation, manufacturing scale-up and commercialisation, subject to the agreement of applicable commercial terms. The Agreement term is for three years and is cancellable by either party with three months notice.

Beyond carbon fibre prepreg, the collaboration is expected to explore opportunities across thermoplastics, resin concentrates, coatings, elastomers and other advanced materials, broadening the potential applications and commercial reach of First Graphene's graphene technologies.

The Agreement provides First Graphene with an opportunity to leverage UNITEX's material development, engineering and manufacturing capabilities, together with its established international customer network, to accelerate the development and industrialisation of graphene enhanced materials and bring commercially viable products to global markets.

First Graphene Managing Director and CEO, Michael Bell, said:

"Carbon fibre and advanced composites represent an increasingly important growth opportunity for First Graphene, as manufacturers seek innovative ways to improve material performance and deliver greater value to customers.

Our internal development work has demonstrated the potential of graphene to enhance the strength and barrier properties of carbon fibre composites. The next step is translating technical advances into commercially scalable products through partnerships with established manufacturers.

UNITEX brings extensive expertise in materials development, engineering and manufacturing, alongside an established international customer network. This collaboration provides FGR with a strategic pathway into China's composites manufacturing sector and expand its commercial reach across global markets.

Importantly, the opportunity extends well beyond carbon fibre. By combining our respective technical and manufacturing capabilities, we see significant potential to develop graphene-enhanced thermoplastics, coatings and other advanced materials across industrial applications.

This agreement is another important step in our strategy to move graphene innovation from development into commercial markets and expand First Graphene's international presence."

About UNITEX

UNITEX Composite (Ningbo) Co., Ltd., established in 2017 and headquartered in Ningbo, China, is part of UNITEX Group, a global materials technology group specialising in advanced composites and integrated material solutions for a wide range of applications. data.title: Australian employment falls sharply in October, jobless rate hits 5-year high
data.description:
Australian employment fell for a second straight month in October and the jobless rate climbed to a five-year high, a surprisingly soft result that bolstered the case that interest rates have likely reached their peak.

Markets are now certain that the Reserve Bank of Australia is done raising interest rates after five rate hikes this year took the cash rate to an 18-year high of 4.85%. Around 38 basis points of easing is priced in by the end of next year, up sharply from 23 bps before the data. (0#AUDIRPR)

The Australian dollar (AUD=3) was down 0.3% to a 10-month low of $0.6698, while three-year government bond futures (YTTc1) rallied 11 ticks to 95.39, the highest since late August.

The Australian Bureau of Statistics said employment fell by 43,500 in October from September, when it dropped a revised 36,400. Analysts had forecast a rise of around 25,000.

The jobless rate climbed to 4.9%, the highest since October 2021, from 4.7% a month ago. The participation rate dipped to 66.6%, while hours worked fell 0.2%.

The weak data contrasted with a surprise jump in wages that pointed to some persistent inflationary pressures in the economy. The RBA had flagged wage growth as a factor in its decision to raise rates earlier this month, having judged the labour market was tighter than it had previously thought.

However, anecdotal evidence of a broader rise in layoffs is building and the RBA board members who voted against a hike this month had flagged the risk the economy was facing a sharper-than-expected downturn.

Retailer David Jones will cut about 1,500 jobs after its collapse into administration, a union said on Wednesday, joining a string of job losses at Australian firms as the economy slows.

data.title: Japanese bond yields fall on safe-haven demand, lower oil
data.description:
By Satoshi Sugiyama

Japanese government bond (JGB) yields fell on Thursday as investors sought safe-haven assets amid jitters in equity markets and stabilized oil prices eased inflation fears.

Here are a few details:

  • The benchmark 10-year JGB yield (JP10YTN=JBTC) fell 1.5 basis points (bps) to 2.855%. Yields move inversely to bond prices

  • The 20-year JGB yield (JP20YTN=JBTC) slid 2.5bps to 3.755%. The 30-year yield (JP30YTN=JBTC) sank 2.5bps to 4.030%. The 5-year yield (JP5YTN=JBTC) fell 1bp to 2.245%

  • Longer-dated US bond yields eased overnight as oil prices fell and after last week’s sharp run-up. Oil prices settled down more than 1% on Wednesday after US crude and fuel inventories posted larger-than-expected rises, adding to expectations of a supply surplus

  • "Buying is likely to take the lead, supported by lower crude oil prices and higher US Treasuries, but the market is expected to struggle to extend gains as domestic JGB supply-demand conditions and expectations for further BOJ rate hikes weigh," said Takayuki Miyajima, senior economist at Sony Financial Group, in a note

  • On Wednesday, Japan's 20-year government bond yield rose after an auction for bonds with the same maturity drew weak demand, even though yields on most maturities fell

  • Analysts express caution over the supply-and-demand outlook for superlong maturities

  • "Probably because pension funds have been key investors in superlong JGBs, the pullback in demand during the equity market decline is seen as the biggest negative factor," said Ataru Okumura, chief rates strategist at SMBC Nikko Securities, in a note. "If share prices fail to rebound, concerns are likely to persist over upcoming superlong JGB auctions as well"

data.title: Japan Data Preview: Hotter Inflation Expected in October CPI Report
data.description:
Consensus outlook for Mace News

Friday, Nov 20, 2026

0830 JST (2330 GMT/1830 EST Thursday, Nov 19) The Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications releases October CPI.

Mace News median: total CPI +2.6% y/y (range: +2.3% to +2.8%) vs. Sept +2.1%; core CPI (ex-fresh food) +2.4% y/y (range: +2.3% to +2.6%) vs. Sept +2.1%; core-core CPI (ex-fresh food, energy) +2.3% y/y (range: +2.3% to +2.7%) vs. Sept +2.4%

TOKYO (MaceNews) - Japan’s consumer inflation is expected to accelerate in two of the three major readings in October as the uptrend in prices becomes clearer and spreads across a wider range of goods and services, following a similar trend seen in the country’s capital.

After all three key measures of the nationwide consumer price index (CPI) rose above the Bank of Japan’s 2% inflation target in September for the first time in six months, the October readings are expected to show further gains, with two reaching their highest levels in 2026.

Higher energy, metal and other raw material costs, as well as food and beverage prices, are contributing to the increase, with the persistent weakness of the yen further pushing up import costs.

This trend was already evident in the Tokyo CPI, a leading indicator of the nationwide trend. The October reading showed broad-based inflation gains across various items, including food, rent, household consumables, auto insurance, train fares, education and hotel fees.

The core index, which excludes fresh food, is expected to rise 2.4%, compared with 2.1% in September. This would be the highest reading since December 2025, when it rose by the same amount.

The total CPI is projected to rise to 2.6% in October from 2.1% in September, marking its highest level since November 2025, when it increased 2.9%.

Meanwhile, the core-core figure, which excludes fresh food and energy, is expected to decelerate to a 2.3% year-on-year rise in October, compared with a 2.4% increase in the previous month.

data.title: Australia's Jobless Rate Rises to Highest Level Since 2021
data.description:
By James Glynn

SYDNEY--Australia's unemployment rate jumped in October to its highest level since late 2021, highlighting fears that the economy is slowing rapidly due to weak confidence and five interest-rate increases since the start of the year.

Unemployment hit 4.9% in October, up from 4.7% in September, the Australian Bureau of Statistics said Thursday.

The economy lost 43,500 jobs in the month, with part-time employment falling by 40,600.

Higher unemployment will argue strongly for the Reserve Bank of Australia to keep interest rates on hold from here, albeit data on Wednesday showed wages grew at their fastest pace since 2023 in the third quarter.

RBA Gov. Michele Bullock also affirmed this week her view that inflation risks remain skewed to the upside.

Inflation data for October will be released next week, with economists warning that there is a high risk that it will once again surprise on the high side of estimates.

Still, the impact of interest-rate increases this year is becoming increasingly obvious, with lending for new homes collapsing and house prices heading toward record losses.

The RBA has talked about the difficult policy task before, highlighting that elevated inflation remains its main priority.

The bank recently forecast that inflation will remain above target until mid-2028, amid concerns inflation expectations are becoming embedded.

The employment-to-population ratio fell 0.3 percentage point to 63.3%, and the participation rate fell 0.2 percentage point to 66.6%

The number of hours worked fell 0.2% in October, while the underemployment rate fell 0.1 percentage point to 6.2%

-Write to James Glynn at james.glynn@wsj.com
